newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish forces release Germans detained in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish forces release Germans detained in Cyprus.

text.p: Four German tourists detained on Monday after straying into Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus were released after being held for more than four hours, Cyprus police said.
The tourists, three men and a woman, were released after mediation by German diplomats who travelled to the Turkish-held areas of the island on Monday afternoon.

All four, identified as brothers Alexander and Mario Pravida, 26 and 25, Sylvia Firster, 23, and Frank Wittki, 25, were escorted back to the southern government controlled areas of the divided island in the afternoon.
The tourists, who arrived in Cyprus on Friday, were briefly questioned by Greek Cypriot police at the crossing. They did not talk to journalists.

Police sources said the four were arrested after they entered the abandoned village of Achna in the southeast Famagusta area, north of the military-patrolled ceasefire line that splits the island into Greek and Turkish Cypriot sections.

Turkish Cypriot radio quoted Turkish security forces as saying the tourists crossed by foot into Turkish-controlled Cyprus. They were found by soldiers in the grounds of the village church, Turkish Cypriot radio said, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

"We believe that the Greek Cypriots encouraged them to come to the region and that this is a Greek Cypriot provocation. An investigation is being conducted by the Police Directorate General," a security force statement said.
A retired fireman was shot dead by Turkish forces in the same area in October when he entered Turkish-held territory. His relatives said he had been collecting snails at the time.
The killing was one of a series of ceasefire line incidents classed by the United Nations as the most violent since Turkish troops invaded the island 22 years ago.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military regime then ruling Greece. Some 30,000 mainland Turkish troops are stationed on Cyprus.
